findings.title: Coverage compares counts from different database snapshots
findings.description: Ledger totals and raw counts are separate queries on the autocommit connection supplied by `_read`. If ingestion commits between them, coverage compares the old ledger against newly committed trades and falsely reports corruption, exiting 3. Ingestion’s transaction does not prevent this reader-side race. Run the report within a read-only, repeatable-read transaction and add a concurrent-ingestion regression test.

findings.title: Coverage repeatedly scans every aggregate on the event loop
findings.description:
Each `_session_row` expands and scans both complete dictionaries to find one session’s instruments. Across all sessions, this produces quadratic growth and runs synchronously inside `build_coverage`. A local benchmark with 2,520 sessions and 40 instruments took approximately 0.64 seconds for just 100 session rows, exceeding the async synchronous-work limit. Group counts by session once, and offload substantial processing from the event loop.

Tests could not run: the available project Python environment lacks `pytest`.
